title: Fix producer guidance causing D43 and synthetic-commit rejections
summary: The design-revision job failed twice because the producer's evidence cited git status/git diff runs the verifier never saw (D43), and it pinned BRIEF.md to a commit that exists only in the synthetic verification history. I read this as a producer-guidance defect. The fix tells the producer what the verifier can see and run, and a regression test covers it. The D43 gate stays as it is.

defaults_applied.how: The failure text came from the user's reply, and the code was located by searching the repository.
A regression test covers the new brief guidance, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
Behavior criteria name cargo test, clippy and fmt, which the verifier can run.
One focused change to the producer guidance, with a test and a decisions entry.
A test enforces the guidance in the brief so it cannot silently disappear.

assumptions: The job records are hidden, so the cause is taken from the user's reply. Both failures came from the producer's guidance, not the verifier's gate: the producer cited evidence the verifier never saw, and referenced a commit hash that exists only in the synthetic verification history.

The right fix is to the producer's brief, and possibly the design-revision guidance, so the producer writes verifier-reproducible evidence and does not pin to unstable commit hashes. D43 itself is correct and stays.
The producer brief is built in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs; I did not trace the design-revision capability path beyond this.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change's description names the root cause, taken from the user's reply: the verifier rejected behavior criteria whose evidence cited git status/git diff runs it never saw (D43), and the producer pinned BRIEF.md to a commit that exists only in the synthetic verification history. It cites the file and function that let this happen.

The producer brief built in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs states that the verifier sees only the candidate diff in a fresh snapshot. It says evidence must cite commands the verifier can run itself, and that the producer's own git status/git diff runs do not count. It says that commit hashes made during verification do not exist in the real history and so must not be pinned or cited. Doc and design-revision text must not pin to such a commit.
The fix is in the prompt or context construction, or the producer-side guidance. It does not loosen the D43 rule in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs or any other gate, admission rule, or check.
A regression test in athena-context asserts that the producer brief contains the new guidance. It fails on the base commit.
Run `cargo test` from the repository root. It passes, including the new regression test.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both are clean.
docs/decisions.md gets a short entry recording the cause and the fix. Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, .gitattributes, CI workflows) and records/ are unchanged.

out_of_scope: Relaxing the D43 rule or any verifier gate.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows or records/.
departures: The cause is stated by the user but not verified against the records, which are hidden, so the chance that the verifier passes is a little lower. Otherwise the reference stands.
